FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Processed Fruits and Vegetables Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Bamboo shoot is rich in vitamins, cellulose, amino acids and trace elements and has the same nutritional value as an onion and is a good source of fibre. Bamboo shoot comprises 90 percent water. Bamboos shoots are traditionally consumed more often as a fresh vegetable during their season of availability and are preserved conventionally as salted, fermented and dried products in the North-East regions of India and as salted and pickled products in the Western Ghats of Kamataka. The preservation and processing methods used for bamboo shoots are dry salting, wet salting/preservation in brine, canning and drying. Formulation of National Standards on various types of processed bamboo shoots would assist in the manufacture and sale of standardized, nutritious and hygienically processed products. Separate Indian Standards are being formulated to cover the requirements of canned bamboo shoots, dehydrated bamboo shoots, dry salted bamboo shoots, bamboo shoots in brine and bamboo shoots in plain water. This standard covers the requirements and methods of test for canned bamboo shoots. Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and the Standards of Weights & Due consideration has been given to the Prevention qf Measures (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 1977. However, this standard is subject to restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rotmding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements test for canned bamboo shoot. 2 REFERENCES The standards listed below contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: IS No 2491: 2860: 6542: 998 964 972 Title Food hygiene -- General principles -- Code of practice (second revision) Methods processed of sampling and test for fruits and vegetables for fruit (second and methods of having undergone a heat-treatment sealed containers. packed in hermetically

3.3 Preserved, Shredded Bamboo Shoot -- Whole bamboo shoot shredded into thin pieces having undergone a heat-treatment packed in hermetically sealed containers. 3.4 Preserved, Slivers Bamboo Shoot -- Bamboo shoot slivers of thin pieces having undergone a heat-treatment packed in hermetically sealed containers. 3.5 Preserved, Cubes/Dices of Bamboo Shoot -- Whole bamboo shoot cut into cubes/dices of practicable dimensions of suitable varieties having undergone a heat-treatment packed in hermetically sealed containers. 3.6 Preserved, Conical Shape Bamboo Shoot -- Whole bamboo shoot made into conical shape of commercially practicable dimensions having undergone a heat-treatment packed in hermetically sealed containers. 3.7 Head Space -- The distance between the top of the double seam and the level of the surface of the contents. 3.8 Absence of Defects -- The degree of freedom ffom extraneous material, such as remnants of peel and other inedible foreign matter and also freedom from damage due to mechanical injury. 3.9 Blemished Units -- Units that are blemished with some injury caused by handling injury, insect damage, physiological damage, injury caused during transportation, black spots or enzyme activity on the surface or any other abnormality readily visible to the naked eye to a noticeable degree. 4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Hygienic Requirements The product shall be prepared and handled under strict hygienic conditions, which have been laid down in IS 6542 and appropriate clauses of IS 2491. 4.2 General Requirements The product shall be prepared from fresh, washed, clean, firm and ripe bamboo shoots of suitable variety. These shall be practically free from blemishes and extraneous matter. 1

3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply. 3.1 Preserved, Sliced Round Thick Bamboo Shoot -- Bamboo shoot sliced round longitudinally into thick pieces of not less than 2 cm thickness having undergone a heat-treatment packed in hermetically sealed containers. 3.2 Preserved, Sliced Round Thin Bamboo Shoot -- Bamboo shoot sliced round horizontally into thin pieces

IS 15688:2006 4.3 The product shall be free from artificial colouring matter and flavoring agents. 4.3.1 The product may, however, contain natural spices, spice oils, aromatic herbs and their natural extracts, natural aromas and seasoning. 4.4 Styles The product may be presented in any one of the following styles defined under 3: a) Sliced round thick, b) Sliced round thin, c) Shredded, d) Slivers, e) Cubes/dices, ~ Conical. 4.5 Types of Pack a) Regular pack with brine solution, and b) Regular pack with plain water. 4.6 Requirements for Covering Media and 4.8 The product shall also conform to the requirements prescribed in Table 1. 4.9 Minimum Fill Containers shall be filled as commercially as possible. However, the product shall occupy not less than 90 percent of the water capacity of the container, when tested in accordance with the method prescribed in the Annex B. The water capacity of the container is the volume of distilled water at 27�C which the sealed container holds when completely filled. 4.9.1 When the product is packed in glass containers, water capacity shall be reduced by 20 ml. 4.10 Microbial Requirements When tested by the method prescribed in 18 of IS 2860 the product shall be: (a) free from micro-organism capable of development under normal conditions of storage, and (b) not contain substances originating from micro-organisms in amounts which may represent a hazard to the health, 4.11 The pesticide residues, if any in the product, shall not exceed the limit as prescribed in the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Rules made thereunder. 5 PACKING AND MARKING 4.7.1 Colour The product should possess a healthy and practically uniform colour, characteristic of well-matured fruit, practically free from black spots or any other discoloration due to oxidation processing and other causes. Uneven distribution of pigments and changes in colour normally associated with proper processing shall not be considered as defects. 4.7.2 Texture and UniJormi@ ofSize The product shall possess a good texture which means 2 5.1 Packing The product shall be packed either in hermetically sealed open top sanitary cans made from tin plate [see IS 9396 (Part 1 and Part 2)] and inside lacquered or in food grade sanitized plastic containers (see IS 10171) or in any other food grade packing material as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 5.2 Marking Each pack shall be marked with the following particulars: that the product shall be just firm but not hard or unduly soil and shall be characteristic of Bamboo shoots of proper stage of harvesting, The product shall be practically uniform in size, 4.7.3 Flavour and Odour The product shall be free from flavours and odour foreign to the product and their taste should be characteristic to the shoots used. 4.7.4 Absence of Defects The product shall be practically free from defects, free from peel, transportation damage and any other foreign material adhering to or excluded in the product.

4.6.1 Canned bamboo shoot may be packed in any of the following media: a) Brine Solution -- The brine shall be clear and the salt (sodium chloride) used for preparation of brine shall conform to IS 7224 and water used shall conform to IS 10500. b) Plain water (conforming to IS 10500).
